lesson_scope: Related rates on a single curve: use the time-chain, preserve signs and units, differentiate polynomials, reciprocal powers and roots, reverse the time-chain, and solve coordinates from a rate condition.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying dy/dt = (dy/dx)(dx/dt) on a standard quadratic curve.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of the chain rule relating time derivatives dy/dt = dy/dx * dx/dt.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the curve equation with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x + 3$$

Evaluate the gradient at $x = 2$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=2} = 2(2) + 3 = 7$$

Apply the chain rule for related rates:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = 7 \times 4 = 28\text{ units per second}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x + 3$ and evaluates at $x = 2$ to obtain $7$.
Uses $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 7 \times 4$ to obtain $28\text{ units per second}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving for dx/dt given dy/dt by reversing the time-chain.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of reversing the time-chain to solve for dx/dt.

hints: Use the chain rule $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dt} \implies 26 = 13 \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dt} \implies \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2\text{ units per second}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the curve to find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 6x - 5$$

Evaluate the derivative at $x = 3$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=3} = 6(3) - 5 = 13$$

Set up the rate equation and solve for $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies 26 = 13 \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{26}{13} = 2\text{ units per second}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 6x - 5$ and evaluates at $x = 3$ to obtain $13$.
Solves $26 = 13\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ to obtain $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2\text{ units per second}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating dy/dt on a reciprocal function with negative derivative sign.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of preserving signs when finding time rates on reciprocal curves.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the reciprocal equation $y = 12x^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = -12x^{-2} = -\frac{12}{x^2}$$

Evaluate the gradient at $x = 2$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=2} = -\frac{12}{2^2} = -\frac{12}{4} = -3$$

Apply the chain rule to compute $\dfrac{dy}{dt}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = -3 \times 3 = -9\text{ units per second}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{12}{x^2}$ and evaluates at $x = 2$ to get $-3$.
Uses $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -3 \times 3$ to obtain $-9\text{ units per second}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying related rates with a square root chain-rule derivative.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of fractional powers and chain rule in related rate calculations.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate $y = (4x + 9)^{1/2}$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}(4x + 9)^{-1/2} \times 4 = \frac{2}{\sqrt{4x + 9}}$$

Evaluate the derivative at $x = 4$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=4} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{16 + 9}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{25}} = \frac{2}{5}$$

Apply the chain rule to determine $\dfrac{dy}{dt}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{2}{5} \times 5 = 2\text{ units per second}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{4x+9}}$ and evaluates at $x = 4$ to get $\dfrac{2}{5}$.
Uses $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{5} \times 5$ to obtain $2\text{ units per second}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: determining the x-coordinate where coordinate rates are equal (dy/dx = 1).

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of translating rate conditions dy/dt = dx/dt into derivative equations.

hints: When $x$ and $y$ coordinates change at the same rate, $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.
From the chain rule $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dt}$, this implies $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1$.

walkthrough.text:
Relate the rate condition to the gradient $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = 1$$

Differentiate the curve to find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 4x - 7$$

Set the derivative equal to $1$ and solve for $x$:
$$4x - 7 = 1 \implies 4x = 8 \implies x = 2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1$ to form $4x - 7 = 1$.
Solves to obtain $x = 2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving for x where dy/dt = -2 dx/dt on a cubic curve.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of setting dy/dx equal to a given rate ratio.

walkthrough.text:
Translate the rate condition into a gradient condition:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = -2\frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = -2$$

Differentiate the cubic curve:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 5$$

Set the derivative equal to $-2$ and solve for $x > 0$:
$$3x^2 - 5 = -2 \implies 3x^2 = 3 \implies x^2 = 1 \implies x = 1$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2$ to form $3x^2 - 5 = -2$.
Uses $x > 0$ to obtain $x = 1$.

hints: Recall the chain rule relating time derivatives: $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \times \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.
Evaluate the curve gradient at the given instant: $\left.\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=3} = 4(3) - 1 = 11$.
Multiply the evaluated gradient by the rate of change of $x$: $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 11 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{11}{2}\text{ units per second}$.

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the given gradient function at $x = 3$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=3} = 4(3) - 1 = 12 - 1 = 11$$

Apply the chain rule relating time rates of change:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt}$$

Substitute the evaluated gradient and the given $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = 11 \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{11}{2}\text{ units per second} \quad (5.5)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates the gradient as $4(3)-1=11$.
Uses $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=\dfrac{dy}{dx}\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ to obtain $\dfrac{11}{2}\text{ units per second}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: a polynomial gradient is evaluated at one stated coordinate, then the forward time-chain gives a signed y-rate whose direction must be interpreted.

parts.difficulty_reason: Easy: a polynomial gradient is evaluated at one stated coordinate, then the forward time-chain gives a signed y-rate whose direction must be interpreted.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source evaluates a derivative at a negative coordinate and connects it to the sign of the y-rate. This original task uses y = 2x^3 - 5x at x = -1.

hints: Since $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 3 > 0$, state that the $y$-coordinate is increasing.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the curve $y = 2x^3 - 5x$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 6x^2 - 5$$

Evaluate the gradient at $x = -1$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=-1} = 6(-1)^2 - 5 = 6 - 5 = 1$$

Apply the chain rule using $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 3\text{ units per second}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = 1 \times 3 = 3\text{ units per second}$$

Interpret the directional behavior of the $y$-coordinate:
$$\text{Since } \frac{dy}{dt} = 3 > 0, \text{ the } y\text{-coordinate is increasing.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=6x^2-5$.
Evaluates the gradient at $x=-1$ as $1$.
Uses the time-chain to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=3\text{ units per second}$ and states that $y$ is increasing.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: a negative rate of change for y must be correctly signed and divided by the evaluated chain-rule derivative to obtain dx/dt.

parts.difficulty_reason: Medium: requires linear-chain differentiation, setting dy/dt = -30 because y is decreasing, and solving for dx/dt.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source requires interpreting a decreasing rate as negative before reversing the chain rule. This original task uses y = (x-2)^3 + 1.

hints: Since $y$ is decreasing at $30\text{ units per second}$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -30\text{ units per second}$.
Use the chain rule: $-30 = 12 \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dt} \implies \dfrac{dx}{dt} = -\dfrac{30}{12} = -\dfrac{5}{2}\text{ units per second}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the curve $y = (x-2)^3 + 1$ using the linear chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3(x-2)^2 \times 1 = 3(x-2)^2$$

Evaluate the gradient at $x = 4$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=4} = 3(4-2)^2 = 3(2^2) = 12$$
Assign the correct sign to the decreasing $y$-rate: $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -30\text{ units per second}$.

Solve for $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ using the chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies -30 = 12 \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dx}{dt} = -\frac{30}{12} = -\frac{5}{2}\text{ units per second}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3(x-2)^2$.
Evaluates the gradient at $x=4$ as $12$ and forms $-30=12\dfrac{dx}{dt}$.
Solves to obtain $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-\dfrac52\text{ units per second}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: fractional power differentiation with an inner linear multiplier must be evaluated and inverted to find dx/dt.

parts.difficulty_reason: Medium: applies fractional power derivative and solves dx/dt from dy/dt.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source combines 3/2 fractional power differentiation with reversing the chain rule. This original task uses y = (2x-1)^(3/2) at x = 5.

hints: Set up the rate equation: $18 = 9 \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dt} \implies \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{18}{9} = 2\text{ units per second}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate $y = (2x-1)^{3/2}$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3}{2}(2x-1)^{1/2} \times 2 = 3\sqrt{2x-1}$$

Evaluate the gradient at $x = 5$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=5} = 3\sqrt{2(5) - 1} = 3\sqrt{9} = 3 \times 3 = 9$$

Solve for $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ using $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 18\text{ units per second}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies 18 = 9 \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dx}{dt} = 2\text{ units per second}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3(2x-1)^{1/2}$.
Evaluates the gradient at $x=5$ as $9$.
Rearranges $18=9\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ to obtain $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2\text{ units per second}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: a relative rate condition between y and x must be converted into a numerical gradient value, then solved for x on a radical curve.

parts.difficulty_reason: Medium: translates relative rate statement to dy/dx = -1/2 and solves a radical equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source sets up a proportional relationship between dy/dt and dx/dt and solves for the coordinate. This original task uses y = 6 - sqrt(2x+1).

hints: Since $y$ is decreasing at half the rate that $x$ is increasing, $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{dx}{dt} \implies \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Translate the proportional rate condition into a gradient value:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{1}{2}\frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{1}{2}$$

Differentiate the curve $y = 6 - (2x+1)^{1/2}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{1}{2}(2x+1)^{-1/2} \times 2 = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+1}}$$

Equate the derivative to $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ and solve for $x$:
$$-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+1}} = -\frac{1}{2} \implies \sqrt{2x+1} = 2$$
$$2x + 1 = 4 \implies 2x = 3 \implies x = \frac{3}{2}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the rate condition to state $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac12$.
Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-(2x+1)^{-1/2}$.
Solves $-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2x+1}}=-\dfrac12$ to obtain $\sqrt{2x+1}=2$.
States $x=\dfrac32$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: setting dy/dt = 0 when dx/dt is non-zero implies dy/dx = 0; differentiating a composite quartic yields a cubic that must be factorised for all exact roots.

parts.difficulty_reason: Hard: deduces dy/dx = 0 from stationary y-rate and solves cubic factorisation for three exact surd values.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source combines a stationary y-rate condition with a quartic derivative to find multiple x-values. This original task uses y = 1/4(x-2)^4 - 7/2(x-2)^2.

hints: Solve the factors: $x - 2 = 0 \implies x = 2$, or $(x-2)^2 = 7 \implies x - 2 = \pm\sqrt{7} \implies x = 2 \pm \sqrt{7}$.

walkthrough.text:
Deduce the gradient condition from the rate information:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = 0 \quad \text{with } \frac{dx}{dt} \ne 0 \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = 0$$

Differentiate the curve $y = \frac{1}{4}(x-2)^4 - \frac{7}{2}(x-2)^2$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = (x-2)^3 - 7(x-2)$$

Factorise the derivative expression completely:
$$(x-2)\left[(x-2)^2 - 7\right] = 0$$

Solve for all possible real values of $x$:
$$x - 2 = 0 \implies x = 2$$
$$(x - 2)^2 = 7 \implies x - 2 = \pm\sqrt{7} \implies x = 2 - \sqrt{7} \quad \text{or} \quad x = 2 + \sqrt{7}$$
$$\text{Values: } x = 2 - \sqrt{7}, \quad 2, \quad 2 + \sqrt{7}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$ and the non-zero x-rate to state $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$.
Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(x-2)^3-7(x-2)$.
Extracts the common factor to form $(x-2)[(x-2)^2-7]=0$.
Solves the resulting linear factor and quadratic equation.
States all three values of $x$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: two-part question requiring recovering a parameter from a signed rate ratio, then finding multiple stationary values from the factorised derivative.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source recovers an unknown polynomial parameter from a signed rate ratio. This original task uses y = (x-2)^4 + a(x-2)^2.

hints: Since $y$ is decreasing at eight times the rate $x$ is increasing, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -8$.

walkthrough.text:
Translate the rate condition at $x = 3$ into a derivative value:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = -8\frac{dx}{dt} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = -8$$

Differentiate the curve $y = (x-2)^4 + a(x-2)^2$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 4(x-2)^3 + 2a(x-2)$$

Substitute $x = 3$ and equate to $-8$:
$$4(3-2)^3 + 2a(3-2) = -8 \implies 4(1) + 2a(1) = -8 \implies 4 + 2a = -8$$

Solve for the parameter $a$:
$$2a = -12 \implies a = -6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the signed rate condition to state $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-8$.
Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=4(x-2)^3+2a(x-2)$.
Evaluates at $x=3$ to obtain $4+2a=-8$.
Solves to obtain $a=-6$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding stationary x-coordinates after substituting the recovered parameter into the derivative.

walkthrough.text:
Set the derivative equal to zero for a stationary $y$-rate with non-zero $x$-rate:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$$

Substitute $a = -6$ into the derivative formula:
$$4(x-2)^3 - 12(x-2) = 0$$

Factorise the cubic expression:
$$4(x-2)\left[(x-2)^2 - 3\right] = 0$$

Solve for all possible values of $x$:
$$x - 2 = 0 \implies x = 2$$
$$(x - 2)^2 = 3 \implies x - 2 = \pm\sqrt{3} \implies x = 2 - \sqrt{3} \quad \text{or} \quad x = 2 + \sqrt{3}$$
$$\text{Solutions: } x = 2, \quad 2 - \sqrt{3}, \quad 2 + \sqrt{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the stationary rate and non-zero x-rate to state $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$.
Substitutes $a=-6$ into the derivative from part (a) to form $4(x-2)^3-12(x-2)=0$.
Solves to obtain $x-2=0$ or $x-2=\pm\sqrt3$.
States all three possible values of $x$.
